_comment: Ratchet baseline for the Datastore Isolation workflow (TD-881).
max_gated is a CEILING THAT MAY ONLY EVER FALL. CI fails when a run exceeds
it, which is the signal that something new in the suite reaches the
operator's real services. When a run comes in under it, lower this number so
the ground gained cannot be given back.
The gated number is data-carrying connections PLUS connections the classifier
could not decide. Undecided ones are included deliberately: a connection that
did not declare itself inside the budget might have carried data, and scoring
it as a harmless probe would let a real regression hide behind a slow runner.
See Tripwire._classify. Bare probes -- a peer that closed having sent nothing
-- are a definite outcome and are not gated.
It is not zero, and that is deliberate. Zero would require every test that
spawns a real hook script to be re-pointed at a throwaway instance -- roughly
eighteen more files, tracked separately as a burn-down. What protects the
operator today is the network namespace: every one of these connections lands
on the tripwire inside the namespace and reaches nothing real. This number
measures test hygiene; the namespace provides the safety.
Before this work the same measurement was 147 accepts / 122 data-carrying
across the three ports then being watched, with 101 on the Qdrant REST port
that tests write through. That port now sits at 4. The total rose only
because Langfuse (23100) was added to the watched set and turned out to
account for 204 connections that had never been measured before.
Two gates. max_gated is the whole-suite total and carries headroom, because
the gRPC retry count moves run to run and a flaky gate gets ignored. Three
consecutive local runs measured 238 / 239 / 240 (data-carrying stable at 228;
the movement is all in unclassified, tracking 26351). A CI runner may sit
higher: slower classification turns definite outcomes into unclassified ones,
which is the conservative direction by design. Set this from the first green
CI run rather than raising it blindly if it trips.
max_per_port is the tight half. 26350 is the Qdrant REST port -- the one
tests actually write through -- and it does not move off 4. Gating it exactly
means a new test reaching the datastore fails immediately, even though the
total has enough slack to hide a handful of connections.
Measured on the CI-scope suite (-m 'not regression and not quarantine') with
a cleared environment, inside unshare -rn, ordering fixed via -p no:randomly.

pre_fix_reference.note: Same command before this work; 23100 was not yet watched.
